text: Welsh broadcaster and author Teleri Bevan (1931–2020; aged 89) was the founding editor of BBC Radio Wales and authored three nonfiction books, including Esmé: Guardian of Snowdonia (2014), a biography of Welsh conservationist Esmé Kirby. Born near Aberystwyth in Wales in 1931, she studied at Bangor University in Bangor, Wales. Bevan began working for the BBC in 1955, serving as a presenter, producer, and editor. In 1978, she was appointed the first editor of BBC Radio Wales, a move that sparked controversy due to the cancellation of the popular programme Good Morning Wales and its replacement with a new morning programme called AM; however, she eventually gained greater popularity. In 1981, she became deputy head of programmes, and in 1985, she advanced to head of programmes for BBC Wales. Throughout her career, she interviewed notable figures such as Tom Jones and Indira Gandhi. After retiring from broadcasting, she pursued a second career in nonfiction writing. In 2004, she published Years on Air: Living with the BBC, a memoir of her broadcasting career. Her second book, The Ladies of Blaenwern (2010), chronicled the history of the Welsh musical group The Dorian Trio and was nominated for the January Book of the Month by the Welsh Books Council. In 2014, she released Esmé: Guardian of Snowdonia. Bevan passed away in November 2020.
